newsitem.title: INDIA: India Reliance first half stuns market.
newsitem.headline: India Reliance first half stuns market.

text.p: India's top private firm Reliance Industries stunned stock markets on Friday by announcing a three percent rise in interim profits against market expectations of a sharp fall, analysts said.
"I'm surprised," said analyst Prakash Joshi at securities firm W.I. Carr.

Analysts said the most obvious reason the net profit of Reliance rose three percent in the six months ended September 30, 1996 to 6.51 billion rupees against 6.33 billion was because the firm did not make any provisions for taxation.
Reliance was expected to provide for a 12.9 percent minimum alternate tax announced in India's 1996/97 budget in July.

"In view of the substantial ongoing capital expenditure programme, the company has been advised that its income tax liability will be determinable only at the year end," the company said in a statement.
"Therefore, provision for taxation, as applicable, will be made at the end of the year." it said.
Joshi said operating margins in the first half of 1996/97 was firm at 19.5 percent against 19.3 a year ago.
"We were expecting operating margins to come down to around 17.3 percent," he said, adding low interest costs had also boosted profits.
"I couldn't believe this," said an analyst at a foreign broking firm. "The margins they're talking about appears on the higher side ... we expected a drop."
He said prices of the company's products had fallen substantially. "It foxes me how the margins stayed nearly unchanged."
Global prices of polyester have fallen more than 30 percent during April-September 1996, against the year ago.
A Reuter poll of 14 leading securities firms last month forecast a 25.8 percent drop in the firm's net profit to an average 4.7 billion rupees.
Sales were forecast to fall 21.1 percent to an average 31.28 billion rupees. Reliance said on Friday its sales during the first six months rose to 40.41 billion rupees from 39.66 billion a year ago.
